review_notes: I read the whole file and compared it with the sibling ModuleCat API in Mathlib/Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Basic.lean and Semi.lean. I also read the uses of these lemmas in Mathlib/RingTheory/Depth/Basic.lean and Rep/Basic.lean. I did not run Lean. The only simp problem I found is the missing `@[simp]` on the `of` iff lemmas. Adding simp to `isZero_iff_subsingleton` would be riskier, because it would match any `IsZero G` goal, so I did not propose it. The four `isZero_of_subsingleton` and `subsingleton_of_isZero` declarations are not natural simp lemmas. I am less sure that no downstream simp set would clash with the new lemma: the ModuleCat precedent suggests not, but I checked no Grp-specific simp calls beyond the Depth uses.

findings.declaration: GrpCat.isZero_of_iff_subsingleton (and the parallel CommGrpCat.isZero_of_iff_subsingleton, with their additive versions)
findings.excerpt:
lemma isZero_of_iff_subsingleton {G : Type*} [Group G] :
    Limits.IsZero (GrpCat.of G) ↔ Subsingleton G :=
  isZero_iff_subsingleton
findings.problem: The lemma `IsZero (of G) ↔ Subsingleton G` is the canonical bundled-to-unbundled form of `IsZero` for a group of the shape `of G`. It carries no `@[simp]` attribute, in both the Grp and CommGrp namespaces (lines 79–82) and in their additive versions. The ModuleCat analogue is already simp, so the two APIs are inconsistent. The only related lemma, `isZero_iff_subsingleton`, has a bundled right-hand side `Subsingleton ↑G`. Because of this, `simp` cannot turn `IsZero (AddCommGrpCat.of (Ext ..))` into `Subsingleton (Ext ..)`. Downstream code must name the lemma instead: Depth/Basic.lean uses `AddCommGrpCat.isZero_of_iff_subsingleton.mpr ...` many times, and also `simp only [AddCommGrpCat.isZero_iff_subsingleton] at zero2 ⊢`.
findings.proposed_change: Add `@[simp]` to the `of` lemmas, matching ModuleCat: `@[to_additive (attr := simp)] lemma isZero_of_iff_subsingleton ...` in both the `GrpCat` and `CommGrpCat` namespaces. Leave `isZero_iff_subsingleton` non-simp, since it matches every `IsZero G` and has no `of` normal form. The left-hand side `IsZero (of G)` is a distinct pattern, and the right-hand side `Subsingleton G` is strictly simpler, so there is no loop risk.
findings.benefit: Goals and hypotheses of the form `IsZero (AddCommGrpCat.of A)`, which are common for Ext groups, would simplify to `Subsingleton A` with plain `simp`. Proofs such as the `have zero2 := ...mpr` plus `simp only [...isZero_iff_subsingleton]` pattern in Depth/Basic.lean could use `simpa` or `simp`. The Grp-valued categories would then match ModuleCat in how they simplify.

evidence.excerpt:
@[simp]
lemma isZero_of_iff_subsingleton {M : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M] :
    IsZero (of R M) ↔ Subsingleton M := isZero_iff_subsingleton
